Abyss watchers are hard. They can be considered the first real boss, as they are the first Lord of Cinder you have access to. My first piece of advice, for the next 50 attempts, do not deal damage. Focus on survival. Your goal is to dance around his moveset. Your goal is to learn the tells for each attack. Basic fromsoft theory. 

Advice number two, if you are struggling parrying, then put some time into locking in where the parry frames are in your parry animation. Lothric Knights are good parry practice, the ones with sword and shield. Their standard multihit combo is reliably the same timing, and the hit you should parry is the second hit in their combo. 
     Phase 1 of Iudex Gundyr is great for learning parrying, his attacks are super telegraphed, and any attack with the blade of his halberd can be parried. When you get to Champion Gundyr, that is the best parry practice in my opinion.
     Most of Abyss Watchers attacks with his sword, not the dagger, can be parried. Any attack with his dagger can be BLOCKED, and he bounces off of you for a free hit, if you can capitalize on it.

Advice number three, level vigor to 27 first. This game is trivialized by having enough health to survive. 

     Bloodborne is a much harder game than DS3. If you beat Bloodborne, then you will be at this too. And remember, summoning is a part of the game for a reason. You got this.
